facts: The occurrence dates back to 16th July, 1983 at about 12.00 noon in a village called Alipur Barota.

The prosecution case as made out, depicts that the accused wanted to dig a khal forcibly through the field of one Maman Ram, which was objected to and the local Sarpanch was also informed accordingly.

At a meeting, called by the Sarpanch, it was decided that the matter ought to be resolved amicably and by reason therefor the Panchayat consisting of Kurra Ram (PW2), Leela Ram (PW1), Ram Kumar Panch and Bhim Sen (PW4) alongwith deceased Maman Ram and a few other persons proceeded towards the field of the accused.
The Maman Ram, the deceased, was few paces ahead of the other members.

When however the deceased Maman Ram, was near the field of Kundan Singh, the accused came out of the field with a double barrel gun and on seeing Maman Ram, raised a Lalkara to the effect 'pani na dene ka maza chakhata hun'.
The accused thereafter fired a shot from his gun, striking on the chest of the deceased Maman Ram.

The other members of the group on hearing the gun shot, stopped there and immediately thereafter the second shot was fired by the accused and who then left the place running with his gun towards village Aharwan.
issues: Whether the eye witnesses' account regarding the number of shots fired by the appellant on the deceased stand contradicted by medical evidence.
Whether the discrepancies found in the ocular account of two witnesses unless they are so vital, cannot affect the credibility of the evidence of the witnesses.
petitioner_arguments: The accused alleged false implication in the case at the instance of Bhim Sen Sarpanch by reason of his brother Ramji Lal having contested an election against Bhim Sen.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution examined nine witnesses in all, and in the statement u/s. 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the accused alleged false implication in the case at the instance of Bhim Sen Sarpanch by reason of his brother Ramji Lal having contested an election against Bhim Sen.
court_reasoning: The positive case of the prosecution as set up by Leela Ram and Ram Kumar, eye-witnesses is that two shots were fired by Om Prakash, appellant at Maman (deceased).
They do not seem to be clear about the site of the first injury.
According to Leela Ram, it has hit on the left shoulder and Kurra Ram's position was that it had hit the left upper arm, near the arm pit.
The injury was on the medial and upper end of left upper arm and its exit was on the lateral side.
To describe in a more simple language, the wound of entry was on the inner side of the left arm. The exit wound was just opposite, that is outer side of the arm.

The shot which was from a close range had entered the chest of Maman (deceased) at the point of strike, after encountering the bony resistence, it appears, the pellets got scattered into two groups; one group which was forcing the overshot cardboard the point which was noted as injury No. 5 by Dr. Chaudhary.

The other group, after bony resistence, split from the main charge and traveled to the left side. After puncturing the heart, it went out at point No. 2 and re-entered the left arm under the arm-pit to make an exit on the lateral side of the left arm.
holding: We are, therefore, satisfied that these injuries on the dead body of Maman were the result of one gunshot and not of two shots, as stated by the eye-witnesses.
